Per Justice G.S. Ahluwalia, This revision is pending since 1999.
None appears for the applicant.
Smt. Sushila Paliwal, Advocate, who is in the panel of Advocates prepared by Legal Aid Committee and has a vast experience of arguing the criminal matters, is present in the Court.
She was requested to argue on behalf of the applicant.
Smt. Sushila Paliwal, Advocate, accepted the request made by the Court.
She after going through the record, argued the matter on behalf of the applicant.

This Criminal Revision under Sections 397, 401 of Cr.P.C. has been filed against the Judgment and sentence dated 20-9- 1999 passed by 8th A.S.J., Bhopal in Criminal Appeal No.91/1998 affirming the judgment and sentence dated 7-7-1998 passed by A.C.J.M., Bhopal in Criminal Case No.3109 of 1996 by which the 2 Criminal Revision No.1527/1999 [Munna Lal Vs. State of M.P. and another]
applicant has been convicted under Section 7(1) read with Section 16(1)(a) (i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and has been sentenced to undergo the rigorous imprisonment of six months and a fine of Rs.1000/- with default imprisonment.
The necessary facts for the disposal of the present revision in short are that on 25-4-1989, the applicant was going to sell the milk and at that time, the Food Inspector, was told by him that his both containers are having buffalo milk and he is a retailer.

sentences.text: The milk was equally distributed and stored in three dry and clean glass bottles and in every bottles, 20 drops of formalin were added and were sealed after affixing labels on them.
One sample was sent to Public Analyst with sample of seal.
The milk was found adulterated and after obtaining permission for prosecution, complaint was filed against the applicant.
The applicant abjured his guilt and pleaded not guilty.

The Trial Court after considering the oral as well as documentary evidence, convicted the applicant for offence under Section 7(1) read with Section 16(1)(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced him to undergo the rigorous imprisonment of 6 months and a fine of Rs.1000/- with default imprisonment.

Being aggrieved by the judgment passed by the Trial Court, the applicant filed a criminal appeal,
which too suffered dismissal by Judgment dated 20-9-1999 passed by Sessions Judge Bhopal in Criminal Appeal No.91/1998.

It is submitted by the Counsel for the applicant that the Trial Court has not appreciated the evidence, which has come on record, in proper perspective and the incident took place in the year 1989 and therefore, a lenient view may be adopted while sentencing the applicant.

sentences.text: It is clear from the record that the applicant has not challenged the jurisdiction and authority of the Food Inspector to collect the Milk Samples.

Even otherwise, where the authority and jurisdiction of the Food Inspector is not challenged, it would be presumed that the Food Inspector had acted within his jurisdiction and was competent to collect the samples.

The submission made by the Counsel for the applicant that since, the evidence of G.S. Gour (P.W.1)
is not supported by the independent witnesses, therefore, he should not be believed as he is an interested witness.
However, the Counsel for the applicant could not point out any circumstance which may make the Food Inspector an interested witness.
However, the report of the Public Analyst is dated 31-5-1989, which was received by the applicant on 6-6-1989.
The complaint was filed on 16-1-1990.
Thus, it is clear that the complaint was filed after 7 months and 16 days from the date of the report of the Public Analyst.

Although the applicant did not file any application for re-examination of sample by Central Food Laboratory, but it is clear that he was deprived of his valuable right of getting the sample re-examined by Central Food Laboratory.

This Court in the case of Mohd. Baitulla Vs. State of M.P. reported in ILR (2011) MP 2607 has held as under :
16.

sentences.text: In the present case, if the factual situation is examined, then it would be clear that the complaint was initiated after more than 7 months.
It is true that no hard and fast limitation can be fixed for consideration of deterioration of the sample.
Formalin loses its effect due to heat, and therefore, it is not necessary that on exact completion of six months, formalin may lose its effect.
One-two weeks may be considered as a period of margin.
But in the present case, the complaint was filed before the concerned Magistrate after 7 months and 18 days, therefore, that margin period was also over.
It is also clear from the record that the applicant did not move any application under Section 13(2) of the Act......

sentences.text:
Therefore, in the light of aforesaid orders passed by this Court in the case of Shiv dayal Saligram Tiwari (Supra) and Ram Singh (Supra), this Court has no option except to acquit the applicant,
because his valuable right under Section 13(2) of the Act to get the sample examined from Central Food Laboratory was withheld.
In the present case also, the samples were collected on 25-4- 1989, the report of the Public Analyst was received on 31-5-1989, whereas the complaint was filed on 16-1-1990.
Thus, it is clear that the applicant was deprived of his valuable right of getting the sample re-examined by Central Food Laboratory.
As the applicant was deprived of his valuable right under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, this Court has no alternative but to acquit the applicant.

Accordingly, the applicant is acquitted of the charge under Section 7(1) and 16(1)
(a) (I) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
The Judgment and sentence dated 20-9-1999 passed by 8 th A.S.J., Bhopal in Criminal Appeal No.91/1998 affirming the judgment and sentence dated 7-7-1998 passed by A.C.J.M., Bhopal in Criminal Case No.3109 of 1996,
are hereby set aside.
The applicant is on bail.
His bail bonds and security bonds are discharged.
The fine amount deposited by the applicant before the Trial Court, may be refunded.
The revision succeeds and is allowed.
(G.S. Ahluwalia) Judge Arun* 5 Criminal Revision No.1527/1999 [Munna Lal Vs. State of M.P. and another] 16/11/2017 Smt. Sushila Paliwal, Counsel for the applicant.
